overview: Isolated late Puercan astragali and calcanea attributed to Purgatorius preserve mobile-ankle features used to test arboreality and a primate-side placement.

ecology.diet: Diet not tested by the isolated tarsals
ecology.habitat: Arboreal use inferred from ankle mobility; depositional setting alone is not habitat
ecology.locomotion: Mobile ankle and inverted-foot capability inferred from tarsal form
ecology.bodySize: Small-bodied mammal; mass estimated comparatively, not measured
ecology.guild: Arboreal locomotor interpretation with diet unresolved

evidenceSummary: UCMP 197509 and UCMP 197517 are isolated bones attributed by comparative regressions and matrices; they are not associated with teeth and do not establish crown-Primate membership or direct ancestry.

overview: Part and counterpart of one juvenile skeleton preserve unusually complete anatomy, soft-tissue outline and gut contents, while preparation history and phylogenetic placement require explicit qualification.

ecology.diet: Plant material inferred from preserved gut contents
ecology.habitat: Messel lake ecosystem; habitual microhabitat remains inferred
ecology.locomotion: Arboreal quadrupedal interpretation from hands, feet and limbs
ecology.bodySize: Juvenile individual; adult body size cannot be read directly
ecology.guild: Small arboreal plant-eater inferred from one juvenile

evidenceSummary: PMO 214.214 and WDC-MG-210 are opposite slabs of one skeleton. Fabricated portions of plate B were disclosed, and no feature makes the specimen a demonstrated anthropoid ancestor.

commonNameZh: 狭鼻猴干群萨达猴标本
overview: Holotype SGS-UM 2009-002 is a partial cranium combining crown-catarrhine features with no diagnostic ape or Old World monkey specialization in the published matrix.

ecology.diet: Diet inferred from preserved dentition; direct feeding evidence absent
ecology.habitat: Shumaysi depositional setting; habitual habitat unresolved
ecology.locomotion: Not preserved by the partial cranium
ecology.bodySize: Known from a partial adult cranium; body mass is model dependent
ecology.guild: Dietary guild unresolved beyond dental inference

evidenceSummary: The holotype and a 36-character matrix support a stem-catarrhine test, but the 29–28 Ma age is biochronological and does not directly date the crown split or identify an ancestor.

overview: Separately catalogued Teilhardina dental samples from three correlated PETM sections document a short Asia-to-Europe-to-North-America appearance sequence, not one tracked population or an ancestor chain.

ecology.diet: Dental samples do not directly record diet
ecology.habitat: Section and carbon-isotope context, not habitual habitat
ecology.locomotion: Not preserved by the dental samples
ecology.bodySize: Body mass is not directly estimated from the reported sequence
ecology.guild: Ecological guild remains unresolved from these samples

traits: Dental comparisons across three PETM sections
evidenceSummary: Smith, Rose and Gingerich document the samples, section correlations and dental comparisons on pp. 11223–11227 (Figures 1–3 and Supporting Tables). Species assignments and correlation underpin the sequence, so it is not a direct record of migration, crown membership or a global first appearance.

commonNameZh: 莫罗古猿姿势骨骼样本
overview: Separate shoulder and femoral specimens MUZM 60 and MUZM 80 from Moroto I and II provide a comparative test of early-Miocene hominoid locomotion; they are not an associated skeleton or demonstrated crown-ape ancestor.

ecology.diet: No direct dietary evidence from the two postcranial specimens
ecology.habitat: Moroto locality context; habitual habitat is not directly established
ecology.locomotion: Mixed arboreal repertoire inferred by comparative functional analysis
ecology.bodySize: Postcranial size estimates are comparative and specimen bounded
ecology.guild: Ecological guild remains unresolved beyond locomotor interpretation

traits: Shoulder morphology in the Moroto sample
Femoral morphology in the Moroto sample
evidenceSummary: MacLatchy and colleagues describe and compare MUZM 60 and MUZM 80 across pp. 159–183 (Figures 1–12; Tables 1–10). Their locality attribution, functional reconstruction and hominoid implications are distinct inference steps and do not establish observed behaviour or a direct ancestor.
